units.title: Recycling missed. Rope Walk. Third week.
units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Third week. Boxes out at 06:45, as instructed in last week's council newsletter ('please put boxes out by 07:00'). The lorry came down Chandlers Row at 07:20, turned at the chapel and left. Rope Walk not collected. I rang the number. Option 4, then option 2, then a recording thanking me for my patience, which I no longer have. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Bernard, you have my sympathy and my experience. Weyhaven is no better. The communal bins at Dellow Court went eleven days in August, and when the lorry finally came it took the bins and left the bags that had been stacked beside them for the eleven days. I wrote a letter. I received a leaflet about recycling.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Bernard, I have passed this to the waste team contact I still have from my council days. Again. For everyone else: the council newsletter that went out this morning says the Rope Walk round moves to Thursdays. Please read it before ringing, as the phone menu does not know either.

units.title: Brackwater junction lights. Ongoing.
units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Brackwater junction at 06:10: red both ways for four minutes, then green both ways for one glorious second, then red again. The van behind me flashed his lights. I flashed back. We have a relationship now. Diversion via the mill road adds six minutes and a pothole the size of a bath.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Is the school bus going round by the mill road while these are on? The letter home said 'possible delays', which is what the letter always says. Mine were twenty minutes late this morning and the youngest missed assembly, which she considers a victory.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Bus was on the main road both ways today, I saw it at the stop line behind me at 07:30. Update 18:20: lights stuck red towards Tollinby again, a council van on the verge with a man inside eating a pasty. Not blaming him. It was a good-looking pasty.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Those lights run off a temporary supply from our pole at the end of the reservoir lane. If they're dropping out it's the controller in the grey box, not the power. Before anyone asks. I've had three people ask me in the shop this week and I'm running out of polite ways to say it.

units.title: Morning crossing. Running commentary.
units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Lisle 07:15 left at 07:23 because a removal lorry could not reverse up the ramp. Eight minutes; I timed it. Not complaining, observing. On the other hand, the coffee machine on the upper deck is working for the first time since the clocks changed, which more than makes up for it.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Ewan, 'not complaining, observing' is precisely what you wrote in your Year Five diary about the school dinners. I recognise the style. I also recognise the missing comma before 'I timed it', but I shall let that go, as you are a grown man with a season ticket.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: The coffee machine was fixed by me, on my break, with a teaspoon and a length of fuse wire. It is not on the maintenance schedule and I will deny everything to the office. Enjoy it while it lasts. The boiler in it is older than some of our deckhands.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Mrs Hale, I stand by every word I wrote about the school dinners, comma or no comma. Return crossing tonight: 17:40 from Port Ammet, on time to the minute. Seth, if you are reading, thank you. That was the best bad coffee I have had all year.

units.title: Found: child's blue glove with a dinosaur. Tollinby.
units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Found on the wall by the Tollinby school bus stop: one small blue glove with a green dinosaur on the back. It's now on the railing outside the bakery, at child height, in a sandwich bag against the drizzle. If it's yours, it's waiting. If you have the other one, please reunite them, I can't bear it.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: For anyone worried: the dinosaur glove was still on the bakery railing at three this morning, dry in its bag. It has been joined by a single grey adult sock and a hair bobble. The railing is becoming a small museum of the lost. I walked past it twice, because that is the kind of night it was.

units.title: Kittering Holm. All of it coming down?
units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Saw the notice go up on the harbour board this morning. Whole of the Holm to come down in thirty days. Aye, I know it's private land now. But my father fished that shore and his father before him, and you get used to a thing being there. Anyone know where the wood's going? They're not shipping it to Port Ammet on that little grey boat.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Moved here from Lost and Found, where I don't think it belongs unless someone has mislaid an island. For reference, the council decision is ADC/VEG/0917 and can be inspected at the council offices. Please keep this to the facts, and please don't speculate about named individuals who work for any of the companies involved.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Clearance jobs that far out burn it on site, Bram, nine times out of ten. Shipping's too dear. Speaking of which, if anyone knows who Grieve are subbing to for this one, I've got my chainsaw tickets, my own kit and a van that only needs a bit of persuading in the cold. No job too small. Or too big. Davey.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: For what it's worth, you can see the work from the Point on a clear day. I had the scope on the Holm this afternoon in excellent visibility (pressure 1024 hPa and rising, dew point 2°C) and there's a new clearing by the landing with a camper and what looks like a cabin roof. Looks tidy. I'll keep an eye on it the way I keep an eye on everything, which is to say obsessively.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Genuine question: is this why there were so many lorries on the Gilliver road last week? My eldest's school bus sat behind a low loader for twenty minutes. He said it had 'a whole house' on the back. I assume a cabin. He is eleven and everything is a whole house.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Ardent Vale Holdings. Look them up. No website worth the name, no staff list, registered at a law firm's address in Halvard. I'm not saying anything. I'm asking why a company with no face wants an island with no people, and why the council waved it through without a single councillor seeing it. Just asking questions. Do your research.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: It's trees. On a private island. Somebody bought it and somebody's cutting it down. Half the companies on earth are registered at a lawyer's office. Grow up, Gil. Next thread.

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: wait so there's actually people living out there now?? do they get wifi or is it like a reality show where they have to chop trees for food lol. someone tell them the chippy delivers to the harbour wall, they'd just have to swim the last nine k

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Burning it, then. That'll be a fair glow on a dark night. Davey, lad, if you want work, there's nets to mend in Gilliver that'll pay you in fish and conversation. I'd not be in a hurry to camp on the Holm side myself. Not for any reason. It's just a long way from your own bed.

units.title: Carrow Point light missing a flash?
units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: I count the Carrow light from my front room every evening, as my mother did, and tonight just after ten past five it was giving three flashes and then a long dark instead of four. My mother would have said the light was 'missing a stitch'. Does anybody know whether it is being mended? I don't like to ring the coastguard about a thing that is probably nothing.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Maud, I live half a mile from it, and you're quite right, I counted it too. It's the new lamp array they fitted in the summer. The controller drops a flash when the battery bank is cold, which tonight it is: 4°C on my station at 17:00 and falling. The coastguard know about it. It usually rights itself by midnight once the charge comes up.

units.title: Night workers wanted (for the radio, not for anything worse).
units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: The Sound FM overnight show has a new phone-in on Thursdays: tell us about the job you do while everyone else is asleep. So far we've had a baker, a woman who irons tablecloths for a hotel and a man who checks lobster tanks at the wholesaler. Ring in. It's nicer than it sounds, and the presenter is better at listening than he is at talking.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: I rang the overnight show once, two winters ago, to talk about a book I couldn't bring myself to finish. The presenter read the last page out on air for me. I've never forgotten it. I don't have a job at night, only the night itself, so I may not qualify, but I'll be listening.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Does it count if it isn't a job? I'm out in Brackwater Woods most clear nights with a couple of microphones, recording ambience. Mostly tawny owls, the odd fox, the reservoir outflow if the wind's wrong. Tonight it's frosty and very still, which is ideal. Not sure it would make good radio. Make of it what you will.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: A man alone in the woods at two in the morning with microphones is exactly the kind of caller we want, dunlin. Bring the owls. I promise the presenter won't ask whether you've ever heard anything spooky, because I'll be holding the cable and I'll pull it.

units.title: Market hall roof: which aisle shuts first?
units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Does anyone know which aisle closes first when the market hall roof work starts? My flower stall is under the worst drip in the building, which my chrysanthemums enjoy and my customers don't. If it's ours, I'll need to find somewhere for two buckets of eucalyptus and a cat bed. Pebble comes to work with me on Saturdays.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: The Courier says the north aisle under the clock closes first. I'll check the notice on the doors when I'm in for the papers tomorrow and confirm here. Your stall is on the east side, if I remember the eucalyptus correctly, so you may have a few weeks' grace.

units.title: Power off Tollinby North this morning.
units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Power was off from 09:30 till about 12:40 in Tollinby North. The advance notice was a card through the door, which the dog ate (not the first card, not the last). Freezer survived with the lid kept shut. Question for anyone who knows: is the next planned work on the same line? I'd like to plan the fish fingers.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Same line, different section, and not this month. That was us swapping two cracked insulators and a length of conductor a branch had a go at in the last gale. Fish fingers safe until further notice. Keep the lid shut like you did and a full freezer's good for the best part of a day.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: I was up the pole for that one, sorry about the card. If it helps, the collie at the mill farm barked at me for the entire three hours and then followed the van to the gate like he'd won. Garvey says that's the job: you do the work and the dog takes the credit.

units.title: Stairwell lights between 6 and 8
units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear neighbours, I am writing because the lift is still broken and I took the stairs down for bread at ten past six this morning. Between the eighth floor and the sixth the lights went out, all at once, as they do on the timer. I stopped on the landing to find the rail, and the footsteps behind me carried on for three or four steps more, and then stopped. When the lights came back there was nobody on the stairs above me. I expect it was someone who turned back. I mention it only so people take care in the dark. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Nothing happens on those stairs that doesn't happen in every building with a timer switch. The lights go off. That is what timers are for. What I would like to know is why the lift engineer was booked for 'between eight and six', arrived at a quarter past six, looked at the lift, and left. I timed him. Four minutes.

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Thanks, Irena. I've reported the 6 to 8 lights to Kerrow again, on the same email as the lift so they can't say they didn't see it. Please don't wedge the stair doors open to get more light through. They're fire doors and we get fined, and then the fine gets spent instead of the repair. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Irena, I'll bring your bread up in the morning while the lift is off, so you don't need the stairs that early. Same for anyone above 8, just ask at the counter. Also for everyone: the timer button on 7 sticks. You have to press and hold it for a second or it gives you half the time. H

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: the cardio of doom strikes again lol. honestly the bit between 6 and 8 echoes like mad, if you stop dead your own steps come back off the landing above for a second. still not great at 6am in pitch black. Irena i'll carry your shopping on thursday, put the list under my door

units.title: Lift out of service (again)
units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Lift is out again. Kerrow say the part is ordered and the engineer is booked. If you're on the upper floors and need shopping carried, put your flat number on the sheet on the noticeboard by the post boxes and someone will help. We managed in March, we'll manage now. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: I can carry for 12, 13 and 14 after 21:00 most days. Not mornings, I am at the depot from 06:00. Put me on the sheet please. I come up the stairs every night anyway with my bag so two more bags is no problem. Benedikt 8A (sorry for spelling)

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: For the record: 1. Lift failures this year: 3, in 7 months. 2. Time to repair, previous two: 11 days and 6 days. 3. Mean: 8.5 days. 4. I will carry for floors 10 to 14 on Saturdays, 09:00 to 12:00. 5. I have put this on the sheet as well, in pen.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Big water bottles come in Wednesday. I'll keep some back for the upper floors and sell them at cost while the lift is off. If you can't carry them, leave your flat number and I'll send my nephew up after school. He complains but he's quick. H

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: Hassan you are a hero. carrying a six pack of water up six floors is my entire gym membership right now. put me down on the sheet for weekends, any floor. not 4am though, at 4am i am a man who sleeps. allegedly

units.title: Visitor bays
units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Somebody with a silver estate has been parked across both visitor bays for four days. Not in one bay. Across both, with the line running under the middle of the car like a parting. The bays are marked. The markings are white. I have photographs, and I am not afraid to use them.

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Wendell, please don't post photos of number plates on here. We've talked about this. Leave a polite note on the windscreen like a normal neighbour, and if it's still there at the weekend I'll ask around. Most of the time it's someone's visiting relative who doesn't know the rules. Bev

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: the silver estate is the daughter of the man in 4A i think, she's staying while he gets over his knee op. she goes home at the weekend. i have seen the bays, wendell, and can confirm they are extremely white. very professional lines. ten out of ten

units.title: Parcels in the lobby
units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Note for people expecting parcels. When the lift is broken, our depot policy says drivers can leave parcels in the lobby with a photo. I don't do that, I bring them up if I am in the building. If you find a parcel left in the lobby with your name, it was not me, and please tell the shop so it is not taken.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Any loose parcel I find in the lobby goes behind the counter with the flat number written on a sticky note. Ask at the shop between 6 and 10. If the shop is shut, try again in the morning, not the shutter. The shutter does not know where your parcel is. H

units.title: Cheap windshield that survives coastal wind?
units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Gilliver breakwater, force four, and my foam is useless. The topside mic on my hydrophone rig is just a reference track, but I'd like it to be a reference to something other than wind. Not spending more than the recorder cost. Fur? Home-made? What's working for people near the sea.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: A cage with a three to four centimetre air gap matters more than the fur. Most of what people call wind noise is turbulence right at the capsule, below about 200 Hz. Quick test: blow gently across it at arm's length and compare the low end with and without the cage. Fur on top buys you another few dB, not a miracle.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: headphones on for this one: in-ear binaural mics are hopeless in wind, but a woolly hat pulled down over the ears works better than it has any right to. I walked the Weyhaven seafront in a gale like that and the result is perfectly usable, apart from the bit where I'm laughing at a seagull.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: There's a pinned list of DIY windshield threads under Gear, please search before posting. This one's fine though, because the next answer is going to be the kitchen sieve trick and it's always worth repeating.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Called it, quaver. Home-made fur over a cage made from a kitchen sieve and a bit of garden hose for the rim. Looks ridiculous and works down to about force five if you get the mic low behind a rock. Gain at -12, low cut on at 80 Hz. Make of it what you will.

units.title: Dawn chorus season is over. What's everyone recording now?
units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so now the dawn chorus is properly done, what's everyone recording? I've been doing rain on the metal bike shed at school, which honestly slaps. Also the reservoir at night, which is mostly ducks complaining. Spectrogram of the bike shed later, it has these lovely evenly spaced bands that I think are the roof ribs.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Gilliver harbour at slack water. Prop wash from the early boats, a bilge pump on somebody's timer every twenty minutes, and a seal that breathes like a man getting to the top of a flight of stairs. All of it's pumps, really. Even the seal sounds like a pump.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: edit to my own post because I can't edit: 'slaps' means good, for anyone over thirty, which I am, so I don't know why I said it. also 'evenly spaced bands' should be 'harmonic-looking bands', I've checked and they're not quite even. sorry. ok

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Night ambience in Brackwater Woods. Two omnis on a stand, spaced about a metre, and the dish if something specific is calling. Tawny owls are busy this month. A fox screamed at 01:20 last week, close, and I dropped a lens cap into the leaf litter. Never found it. Heading out tonight; it's frosty and dead still, so the reservoir should be quiet too.

units.title: Housekeeping: raw files, please
units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Housekeeping, as it's the start of a month. Please upload raw files, not phone recordings of your speakers, and give kit, gain and location (roughly is fine; nobody needs your postcode). We are a recordings forum. Stories without files go to the Chat board, where they will be lovingly ignored.

units.title: New month check-in: where are you and what are you drinking?
units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: new month, new check-in thread. Say where you are, what you do and what's in your cup. A reminder that Lamp Hours is for company on the night shift, not campfire stories. Coriveth, night pharmacy counter, peppermint tea that has gone cold twice. The shutter's half down and the street outside is all wet cobbles and one cat.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Coriveth container port, gate 7. Coffee, flask, brewed 22:00. 01:00 patrol of stacks A to F complete. Patrolled, nil found. Two reach stackers parked out of position, logged for the day shift. Will report again at 04:00 if anything happens, which it will not.

units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: Vellmark, residential home, nights. Rooibos. One of our ladies is awake and wants to talk about her sister's wedding, the one where the cake fell over, so I'm listening while I do the charts. She tells it a little differently each time and it gets better every time. Sorry this is short.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Retail park car park, Weyhaven. Control says hi, which he doesn't. Tea from a flask my mum got me with my name on it in big letters, in case another guard steals it, which has happened twice. Route tonight is the same as every night: barrier, loading bays, the dark corner by the garden centre, back to the hut.

units.author: lh_crane_halvard
units.text: Halvard, tower crane, sixty metres up on a night pour. Thermos of lentil soup. From up here the ring road looks like a necklace somebody dropped, and the hospital car park is the only bit lit like daylight. The wind is light, which means I get to enjoy the view instead of holding on to it.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Halvard sleep clinic. Three patients wired up and all three asleep before eleven, which is a personal best for the ward and a mild insult to my bedside manner. Decaf, because I tell people to drink decaf and I'd be a hypocrite. The monitors are the brightest thing in the room.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Harbour bakery, Coriveth. First proving done and the whole street smells of rye and caraway, and I'm sorry for everyone asleep and missing it. Milky coffee out of a measuring jug, don't tell the inspector. Tonight's special is a seeded loaf I'm calling 'the regret', because I forgot the salt on the first batch.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Port Ammet General, portering, B corridor and the run to Imaging. Drinking vending machine hot chocolate, which tastes of the vending machine. Machine 3 on the ground floor gives you two cups if you thump it at the right angle. I'll take that secret to my grave. Or I would have, before I typed it here.

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Halvard, respiratory ward. Water, because I read the sign above the sink that says 'have you had water'. Ward is calm, which we never say out loud, so I'm typing it instead. Bed six snores like a bus pulling away. Back to it.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Sound FM overnight studio, Port Ammet. Producer, so I'm the one who decides which callers get through and which go to the 'thanks for calling' recording. Coffee from the machine that the presenter calls Gerald. Nobody knows why. I've stopped asking.

units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: aisle 41 reporting, distribution park outside Weyhaven. Target tonight is 140 picks an hour, a joke the scanner tells me every 26 seconds. Energy drink, the blue one that tastes like a battery. My heart is fine. My knees have filed a complaint with management.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: Tollinby. Not working, only awake, which I'm told is permitted here. Camomile, which has never once worked and which I drink out of loyalty. I'm reading a novel in which a man spends forty pages deciding whether to post a letter. I feel seen, and slightly hurried.

units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text:
cab 4417 Halvard nights
had a fare tonight who wanted the airport but via his ex's street so he could 'just look at the house' anyway we looked at the house
it was a nice house
cola from the all night garage on the ring road, the one with the broken sign that says ARAGE

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Vellmark. Pump station on level four, all night, one seal that wouldn't. Tea, strong enough to stand a spanner in. On the bus home now. Town's still dark. Shift done.

units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: Tamsin Bay light, one of the last with a keeper. Coffee kept on the stove since dusk, which by now makes it more of a soup. A long swell tonight; from the gallery you can follow every crest the beam touches, out to the point where it stops and the dark carries on without it. Quiet. Good.

units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: Tamsin Bay, utilities helpline, between calls. The hold music is a flute that's been looping since before I started. Coffee, black, regret. First caller of the night wanted to know if their electricity meter 'could hear them'. It can't. I checked the script. The script didn't say, so I checked the meter manual. Still no.

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: Weyhaven bus depot love, doing the insides of the double deckers before the morning lot go out, mostly crisps under the seats and the odd umbrella and once a whole birthday cake still in its box which nobody ever claimed, tea from the depot urn which is older than me and makes everything taste of the urn

units.title: Starting a run of nights? Anchor sleep.
units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Practical note for anyone starting a run of nights: anchor sleep. Four hours at the same clock time every day, working or not, keeps your body clock from drifting all over the place. Dark room, no screens for the first half hour, and something small to eat before bed rather than a full dinner. It isn't glamorous, but it beats the 'I'll just stay up' method, which I have watched fail in a lab.

units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: Anchor sleep saved me in my first year. The other thing is telling your family your hours, in writing, on the fridge door. Otherwise somebody hoovers the landing at noon and asks why you look like that at tea.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Logged. Blackout curtain fitted to bedroom window: two years ago. Result: improved. Earplugs: tried, removed, could hear my own heartbeat, not recommended. Small meal before bed: will trial from tomorrow and report.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: I have the anchor and no ship, as it were. Still, I'll try the small-meal part. Toast is small. Toast with a little honey is small and optimistic. Thank you for writing it out so plainly; it's a kindness to be told what to do at this hour.

units.title: quay prices and the weather
units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Prices today. Cod 4.10 the kilo, haddock 3.60, langoustine fair, crab poor because the Lisle boats all landed at once. Wind's going round west by the morning. Creels on the Holm side came up clean, nothing in them but weed and one very cross dogfish. Fog in the air by the end of the week, I'd say, by the feel of it.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: crab price is a crime lads. chandlery has creel twine back in, 4mm and 6mm, the cheap stuff has gone already so dont ask. also whoever left a bucket of bait on my step this morning thank you and also please dont

units.title: Holm contractor boat on the slip
units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: heads up lads the Holm contractor's boat is using the slip at the top of the tide most days for the next month. grey workboat with a little crane, skipper is from Port Ammet. give him room on the turn. and no he does not want to buy bait, I asked

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Thank you, Rook. The contractor's vessel has a berth booking on the inner wall for thirty days. Under byelaw 14 the top of the slipway must be kept clear of trailers during its movements, which are posted daily on the harbour office board. Please and thank you, everyone.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: we passed it on the 16:00 coming back from Lisle, the skipper waved at us with his whole arm like a man on his holidays. seems happy enough. I'd be happy too if I wasn't getting up at five to coil rope in the dark while someone else gets a crane

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: he's paid per run finn not per wave. if you want a crane get your tickets. if you want a holiday get a different job

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Saw him go out at first light. Low in the water with fuel drums and a pallet of something wrapped in plastic. He didn't stop at the landing long, and I don't blame him, it's a long way round the Holm side with the tide against you. Good boat. Better than he's got any right to on that money.

units.title: Winter night rota
units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Rota for the winter nights is up in the crew room. I'm on the late Gilliver run through the month with Kerris as mate, Finn on deck and Seth below. If you're on the list and want to swap, please do it through the office and not on a beer mat in the Anchor. Checked the slip lights at Gilliver on the last run: two out of six working. Reported it, carried on.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Below for the month as well. The number two genset is sulking about its fuel, so if the deck floods dip on the crossing it's not you, it's a filter. I have a new one on order and a very old one in my pocket for emergencies.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Beer mat swaps are a tradition, skipper. But fine. Late Gilliver run is mine. I'm bringing the good torch from home this time, the big one, because two lights out of six on that slip is a joke and I've nearly gone in twice on the wet bit at the bottom.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: so I'm on deck all month which means I'm the one doing the ropes in the rain while kerris holds the good torch and points it at me like a policeman. noted. fair. fine. someone bring biscuits on the late run, the ones with the jam in, not the plain ones

units.title: Gilliver feeder patrol notes
units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Did a ground patrol along the Gilliver feeder this afternoon with Garvey. Two spans with old gull nests on the crossarms from summer, three trees by the Lisle road that want trimming back before the gales, one stay wire a bit slack near the boatyard. Nothing exciting, which is the right amount of exciting for a line.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: The right amount of exciting is none, Tess. Write it in the book properly so the trimming crew get it this side of the new year, and put the stay wire first because that's the one that'll bite. Good patrol. You looked up more than you looked at your phone, which is the whole job.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: while you lads are here, the chandlery lights flicker every time the ice plant kicks in next door. is that you or me

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: That's you, Rook. That's your ice plant's motor pulling the volts down when it starts. Get an electrician to look at your board before it looks at you. Flaming old boards in those harbour sheds, half of them are held together by paint.
